title: Throughput microtopography: INT8/FP8 kernel heatmap and quality contours
short_summary: Field notebook mapping per-kernel throughput and quality degradation across INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ quantizations. Produces an operational heatmap view (by model, sequence length, kernel impl) and concrete mitigation suggestions for tail and burst workloads.
content:
Context:
This doc collects exploratory notes and field results from a week-long profiling sweep across kernels and quantizations with the explicit goal of creating a single operational view — a "throughput microtopography" — that surfaces where kernels create cliffs (throughput drops) or plateaus (safe zones) and where quantization induces unacceptable quality contours.

Why this felt necessary:
- Many existing bench runs report tokens/sec or avg latency but hide fine-grained topologies: specific kernels (matmul, softmax, rotary) can dominate tail behavior depending on sequence length distribution and KV-cache hit patterns.
- Customers run mixed traffic: short chat vs long-context summarization. We need per-kernel maps so policy routing (fallback to FP16, degrade to smaller model, or change batching) can be automatic.

Experimental scope and constraints:
- Models: small-medium LLaMA-style transformer (7B, 13B) and a distilled 30B (replicate internal field sample).
- Backends: INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric profiles), AWQ (per-channel), GPTQ (4-bit/8-bit fallback), FP8 prototype path.
- Kernels: vendor GEMM (cuBLAS-like), tiled custom matmul, fused attention-softmax, rotary+kv-gather kernels, cache-apply (kv read/write).
- HW: A100 (40G), H100 (80G), RTX 6000 testbed for edge profile.
- Workloads: single-request latency SLO (50ms baseline), burst mix (10k QPS synthetic fanout), long-context streaming (16k tokens), and chat-style short sequences (32–128).
- Metrics collected: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, peak memory bandwidth, GPU occupancy, kernel time per-call, warp efficiency, numerical quality deltas (KL / BLEU-lite / logprobs), and a synthetic prompt-regression score computed from a small eval-set of 400 prompts.

Methodology (brief):
- Controlled replay harness that keeps request mix steady and records per-request kernel traces via Nsight Sampling + our microbench client that annotates request type.
- Kernel attribution done by correlating timeline with nvprof ranges and our lightweight tracer (40us overhead).
- Quality measured offline: decode outputs from quantized run vs FP16 baseline, compute prompt-regression score, track failure modes (truncation, hallucination spikes on targeted prompts).

Key observations (high level):
1) Microtopography exists: throughput heatmaps are not monotonic with sequence length. Example: at 512->1024 tokens many tiling kernels hit a memory-bound cliff, dropping tokens/sec by ~22% for INT8 AWQ kernels while FP8 path maintained ~5% drop.
2) Kernel coupling: fused attention-softmax and kv-apply interactions produce multi-kernel congestion; even when matmul still has headroom, attention kernels serialized and created p95 spikes. This effect is much larger on GPTQ implementations that split attention into smaller kernels (more launches -> more scheduling jitter).
3) Burst sensitivity differs by quant strategy: AWQ reduces compute but increases memory traffic patterns (per-channel scales force extra gathers), which elevates bandwidth utilization and makes throughput worse under burst than steady-state. INT8 symmetric tends to be more predictable under bursts but has higher quality regression on certain prompts.
4) FP8 showed promise as a middle ground for long-context: lower tail amplification and better numerical fidelity than INT8 for our 13B baseline, but at the cost of more kernel-level variability across vendors (H100 optimized FP8 kernels matter).

Selected datapoints (representative):
- 13B model, 1024 tokens, burst mix: INT8-AWQ tokens/sec down 22%; p95 latency +48ms; prompt-regression score down 6.8 pts. FP8 tokens/sec down 6%; p95 +12ms; regression -1.2 pts. GPTQ-8bit showed tokens/sec similar to INT8 but p99 jitter 3x due to micro-launch overheads.
- 7B model, short-chat (64 tokens): INT8 symmetric slightly faster (7% median) with negligible quality change; AWQ and GPTQ similar but higher p99 variance.

Operational heatmap idea (what we built):
- 2D heatmap: x-axis sequence length bucket, y-axis kernel_impl (vendor vs custom fused), cell color=relative tokens/sec loss vs FP16 baseline; cell border thickness encodes prompt-regression delta; hover tooltip includes p95/p99 and memory bandwidth.
- We used this to mark "safe corridors" (cells with <=5% throughput loss and <=1.5 pts regression) and "cliff zones" (>15% throughput loss or >5 pts regression).

Immediate mitigations and playbook entries:
- Routing policy: for requests with predicted long context (>512 tokens) prefer FP8 on H100 if available; fall back to FP16 on mismatch.
- Burst throttle + microbatch shaping: add short-term token budget and split a large request into two scheduled units to avoid simultaneous heavy kernel launches on attention paths.
- Kernel coalescing: upstream change to fuse small GPTQ attention fragments back into larger launches on N=7B/13B to reduce scheduling jitter. PR linked in artifacts.
- Metric guardrails: expose a per-model heatmap alert when a cell enters "cliff zone" for >5 minutes.

Open questions / next runs:
- Repeat the sweep on dedicated multi-tenant nodes to measure cross-tenant interference; hypothesis: bandwidth cliffs amplify under multi-tenancy.
- Add micro-bench for per-layer AWQ gather overhead to isolate whether AWQ cost is from memory patterns vs compute.
- Evaluate decoding strategies (sampling vs greedy) effect on throughput microtopography.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Clean up harness code and move to internal bench repo (PR pending).
- Produce a small interactive dashboard export for Console team (heatmap + drilldowns).
- Verify results on edge NVLink configs and add to public KB.

Appendix (short):
- Tools: Nsight command sampling, nvprof timeline, our microbench client (v0.13), perf counters: DRAM_READ/WRITE, SM_Util, Active_Warps
- Scripts used: run_heatmap_sweep.sh (in linked PR), parse_nvtrace.py, compare_decodes.py

If you want the raw csv slices or the interactive heatmap export I pushed to the bench bucket, ping me or check the linked artifacts. This is a working notebook — expect minor updates as we re-run on multi-tenant hardware.
